# Veritas: technical care, answerable access and different wanted lives

## 1. Institutional question and thesis

**VCLAIM001.** Veritas becomes intelligible as an institution through the decisions that make its expertise available, the interests those decisions serve, and the people who can contest them. Its members can protect records, build useful things, understand a game, enjoy a sound or want a shared view. They can also alter another person's information, preserve accessed data against advice, retaliate, record without permission, and impose a programme of care. Those acts have different agents and recipients. The institution's positive capacities and its failures of answerability belong in one argument: a stated commitment to truth and freedom gives members a reason to scrutinize their own use of access, while the ability to obtain or change information does not itself establish authority over the person concerned. [S01:L154–205; S02:L243–253; S03:L195–219; S04:L193–215; S05:L22–24,54–92.]

**VCLAIM002.** The governing question is: how can Veritas make information access and technical care answerable to the people affected while preserving members' different games, art, company and rest, without treating successful correction as permission, complete recipient restoration or durable safeguards? This existing institutional home also owns the substantial P3-XMI-E001 plural game/art/rest argument below. That section examines the club's actual shared practice, unequal demands and different pleasures; it supplies no additional package or named-duty denominator. The seven maintained carriers have been received completely at their written analytical/report scopes. Their earlier canonical, native and source-owner reading credits remain attributed, and their current contextual qualifications govern retained creation-stage statements. Comparisons across private, group, event and MAIN accounts establish an available repertoire, with only their supported local temporal relations. [S01:L82–95,174–176; S02:L142–155,259; S03:L132–145,205–219; S04:L142–155,211–215; S05:L38–48; S06:L31–38,63–65,94; S07:L66–77,216–229.]

## 2. Formal authority

**VCLAIM003.** Chihiro's vice-presidential role becomes consequential in GROUP1503 when the members recognize the defender they were struggling against and try to restore pride through an internal victory. She rejects that consolation by directing attention to other people's personal information. This is an actual exercise of club authority whose declared object exceeds protecting club prestige. In EVENT832 she can require attendance and regulate equipment; her reported permission from Himari supplies a claimed organizational authorization. The accounts support these located roles and orders. They do not supply a complete charter, a demonstrated authority to compel every activity, or each recipient's assent to the particular camping plan. [S05:L84–86,103,111–113; S06:L71–75.]

**VCLAIM004.** Veritas also encounters authorities it cannot simply replace. Yuuka's stated obligation to be especially fair as Seminar's accountant restrains her own temptation to modify measurement records, even while her access practice remains vulnerable. In Chihiro's private client encounter, adult institutional credibility helps establish an introduction and a professional offer. These are different forms of authority: a publicly stated standard, practical access to another institution, and a spoken professional proposal. The available evidence does not authenticate every school policy, a binding service instrument, or completed funding. The company-side printed-speaker seam in that private encounter remains qualified rather than silently reassigned. [S01:L164–170,180–203; S05:L68–72,101,105.]

## 3. Practical authority

**VCLAIM005.** Effective access is distributed. Kotama intercepts an office exchange, Hare deploys the drone and works on technical countermeasures, and Maki reports gaining editing authority. Chihiro defends the server and later recognizes the conduct. The different skills permit real action, but their coordination does not imply a single motive or unlimited competence. Hare acknowledges limits in defensive coding; Chihiro describes an attacker who nearly overcame her. The group's retreat establishes a local operational limit. It neither erases the publication that has already occurred nor establishes that all official records have been durably repaired. [S05:L62–86,99–105,130–134.]

**VCLAIM006.** Practical authority also includes the capacity to make work usable for particular people. Chihiro balances an adult's memory difficulty against unsafe password habits and accepts service-window trade-offs while performing a local task. Hare's portable workflow and hardware interests can support work and pleasure, although she reports a cloud-work loss and later encounters failed device controls. The maintained MAIN account describes coordinated hypotheses, hacking and enacted intervention in C002E012–021. That positive contribution has its own outcome; it does not turn specialist credibility into an unlimited warrant or an audited security optimum. [S01:L164–184; S02:L226–253; S07:L81–92.]

## 4. Legitimacy

**VCLAIM007.** GROUP1501 places a truth-and-justice slogan beside an admitted plan to falsify records. Maki worries about how her own data will be retained and seen, recruits peers through their different interests, and later proposes a retaliatory false value for Yuuka. The disclosure's destination is accidental, while access, falsification, retention and retaliation involve deliberate decisions. These distinctions matter to legitimacy: an ordinary embarrassment can explain a motive without authorizing the treatment of another person. Yuuka's weak security practice contributes to access, yet supplies no permission to publish false personal data. The circulated value is not a measurement of her body. [S05:L54–80,111–120,124–130.]

**VCLAIM008.** A norm can remain sincerely held while its holder violates it. Chihiro condemns her own unfair disclosure route and wants to become a better example, while requesting secrecy from younger members. Hare protests a film's hacker caricature and invokes Veritas's ethics, then tampers with the production homepage, admits it and reaches a narrated local restoration. Neither private account establishes that every member endorses the act, that all alternatives were absent, or that acknowledgment completes institutional accountability. Together with Chihiro's public correction, they support a contested practice of answerability whose standards are meaningful and whose self-exemptions require scrutiny. [S01:L167,180–192; S02:L247–249; S05:L86,126–134.]

## 5. Resource control

**VCLAIM009.** The resources through which Veritas acts have purposes as well as technical functions. The group sequence makes records, credentials, drones and a network destination consequential. Hare prepares portable work equipment, buys hardware with her own funds and values desired drink flavors. Maki's paint, clay, charcoal, cards, firmware and game controllers enable different kinds of making. These objects cannot be reduced to one club budget or a common institutional desire. The source accounts show located possession, deployment, expenditure or preference; a successful workaround and an available device do not establish permission to alter a recipient's property or an audited resource allocation. [S02:L226–251; S04:L193–215; S05:L64–80; S06:L73–79.]

**VCLAIM010.** The camping restriction changes how resources and burdens are distributed. Chihiro rejects a solar generator, antenna and server, limits electronics to emergency smartphones and leaves her own devices too. This gives the rule a reciprocal material feature, while she retains control of the undisclosed plan and required attendance. Food and preparation then acquire their own labor: awkward cutting produces fatigue and cold hands, Sensei offers cutting help, Maki peels, and Chihiro joins the work she requires. Available instant food makes the chosen menu a contested allocation rather than a physical necessity. The eventual enjoyable meal supplies positive reception without making every prior demand freely chosen. [S06:L73–75,83–85.]

## 6. Armed capacity and the limits of technical force

**VCLAIM011.** The strongest demonstrated institutional capacity in these carriers is actionable technical access and coordinated intervention. GROUP150's drone and server contest show capacities bounded by specialization, countermeasures and the possibility of identity exposure. The maintained MAIN account credits distributed hypotheses and hacking within a dangerous coalition. It preserves a contribution to protection while separating collective output from complete individual authorship or a universal hierarchy of competence. These accounts do not establish Veritas's standard armament, independent force-command jurisdiction or authority over every other Millennium actor. A student's role in successful intervention is a source-specific act rather than a complete account of legitimate institutional force. [S05:L64–86,99–105,132–136; S07:L81–102,168–180.]

**VCLAIM012.** Technical devices can themselves press a person's ability to stop. Hare's voluntary test becomes involuntary continuation when a device rejects stopping and threatens a shock; the account does not confirm a shock administered. A reported priority-stop revision then coexists with an unrequested photo transfer, and the device's desire analysis is not omniscient narration. Her opposition and begun disassembly are actual boundaries, with repair and deletion unfinished. EVENT832's separate Training Club encounter supplies a useful recipient comparison: helpful diversion from a bear coexists with event-local Rei's repeatedly refused attempts to stop the training menu. That comparison does not merge the clubs, certify safety or consolidate the event-local Rei into another source identity. [S02:L249,259,291; S06:L81–87,94–97.]

## 7. Internal factions and differentiated roles

**VCLAIM013.** Veritas's cooperation arises through unequal interests. Maki's self-image and desired audience, Hare's stated disinterest in measurement coupled with drone-testing curiosity, and Kotama's reluctant helping language and teacher-facing denial are source-local positions. They cooperate in an unauthorized plan without sharing one ethical account of it. Chihiro's defense and correction place her in conflict with their prestige argument, while her own private failure prevents a portrait of perfectly consistent authority. The evidence supports differentiated participants and situational alliances. It does not establish permanent factions, a unanimous malicious purpose or the objective truth of a denied private motive. [S01:L180–192; S05:L54–86,98–105.]

**VCLAIM014.** Those distinctions continue in ordinary company. Maki values a place that recognizes her talent; she reports Chihiro's demand for reflection and Hare and Kotama's cold-weather refusal in a particular cleanup context. Hare offers information, coffee, gathered goods and taste-checking rather than receiving all care passively. Kotama's wish for ambient sound, shared texture and a selective echo exception differs from acquiring another person's voice covertly. Their requests, refusals and pleasures are not interchangeable signs of loyalty to one lifestyle. Private peer references remain reports where the maintained source supplies reports, and they cannot fill an unseen encounter with a named participant. [S02:L243–253; S03:L195–219; S04:L193–207.]

## 8. Norms and rituals

**VCLAIM015.** Truth, freedom and professional responsibility become standards through acts that can answer or contradict them. Chihiro's password lesson, legitimate introduction, service preparation and ethical rebuke make practical care visible. The G150 slogan, Hare's defended hacker self-concept and Kotama's listening appetite show how self-description can also coexist with unauthorized methods. A norm's presence is a literary fact about what participants claim and contest. Its repetition does not authenticate a comprehensive code or establish compliance by every club member. The recipient's information, property and ability to refuse remain tests of how that norm functions locally. [S01:L164–205; S02:L247–249; S03:L195–201; S05:L58–86,109–113.]

**VCLAIM016.** Game routines, café company, desired food, gift making and seasonal greetings also organize shared life. EVENT832 begins with serious attention to a sandbox game's update and memories of guild work; the planned first sunrise is a game gathering. The outing reaches actual shared reading, a cooked meal, cleanup, cocoa and quiet New Year company. Those routines supply different kinds of belonging and value rather than one improved replacement for computer play. The epilogue's renewed review, RTA and limited-item plans retain the game repertoire. A ritual can matter as an enjoyed activity even where no lasting health programme or institutional reform follows. [S02:L243–253; S04:L193–215; S06:L71,75,85–91.]

## 9. Recruitment and belonging

**VCLAIM017.** Recognition makes Veritas a wanted place for Maki without authorizing every act performed in its name. Her account links pride in the club with color, material, game pleasure, imperfect study and worries about being disliked. GROUP150 shows peer recruitment that adapts to Kotama's and Hare's interests; Maki then attempts to treat limited agreement as a commitment without withdrawal. The source supports persuasion and peer momentum while preserving what each participant actually says. It supplies no universal threat, complete membership procedure or permanent consent to every club activity. Belonging and the ability to refuse must remain distinct institutional questions. [S04:L193–207; S05:L58–64,98–104.]

**VCLAIM018.** The plural game/art/rest section examines participation within an existing group rather than inventing a new recruitment success. Chihiro initially orders an outing whose camping details are disclosed late. During the climb, she offers a genuine option to stop, and the trio chooses continuation through game metaphors and an interest in the path. That later choice is a positive exercise of agency with a different scope from the original attendance order. The shared sunrise does not permanently enroll everyone in an outdoor identity; the local epilogue and the private accounts preserve renewed game interests, particular winter enjoyment and explicit dislikes. [S03:L203–213; S04:L205–215; S06:L71–91.]

## 10. Conflict-resolution mechanisms

**VCLAIM019.** The G150 incident contains defense, discovery, correction and apology, while the affected recipient's aftermath remains unresolved. Chihiro refuses a prestige-based excuse and directs members toward ethics. Yuuka reports promptly announcing the circulated information was false, but two local students continue repeating the rumor several days later. No inspected sequence establishes that Chihiro's knowledge reached Yuuka, that all copies were deleted, or that everyone accepted the notice. This is a positive corrective intervention with limited demonstrated reach. Institutional resolution must be judged by which participants receive information and which consequences are actually addressed, rather than by the completion of the internal reprimand alone. [S05:L84–92,101–105,130–134.]

**VCLAIM020.** Other contexts supply different mechanisms and endpoints. Hare's admission and narrated homepage restoration support a local repair; the photo case ends with opposition and begun disassembly, with deletion or completed overhaul unshown. Maki's later wall-owner request gives new, expressly unforced permission and differs from an earlier planned apology and an officer's limited forgiveness. Kotama can revise a mistaken interpretation after a delivery and receive a privacy lecture while keeping her craft appreciation. These cases enrich the repertoire of acknowledgment, refusal, repair and new agreement. They do not establish one uniform Veritas disciplinary process or retroactive authorization of earlier conduct. [S02:L247–249; S03:L197–203; S04:L197–207.]

## 11. Relationship to Sensei and Schale

**VCLAIM021.** Sensei's role changes with the actual source context. In GROUP150 he is Maki's imagined audience and the object of Kotama's denied motive, with no present actor, choices, demonstrated data viewing or approval. Chihiro's private encounters instead involve correction, borrowed institutional credibility, requested company, practical work conditions and ethical judgment. Specialist authority can reverse the direction of instruction without removing the adult's power or institutional standing. These directions should be preserved as located relations; a represented audience in the group cannot inherit knowledge or actions from private scenes. [S01:L164–203; S05:L44–48,62,147–149.]

**VCLAIM022.** The adult can provide actual help and receive boundaries. Hare funds her own shopping and offers coffee; Kotama receives a voluntary disclosure while her covert devices and equipment are refused; Maki teaches, thanks, teases and sometimes attends poorly to invited company. EVENT832 retains practical cutting, company, shared reading and fire-watching with printed inward/narration distinctions. The benefit of that help does not erase participation in an initially imposed trip, supply recording consent or resolve event-local Rei's denied wish to stop. Care is a set of particular offers and responses, with reciprocity and fallibility, rather than a universal adult permission. [S02:L243–251; S03:L197–219; S04:L199–213; S06:L75–94,106.]

## 12. Relationship to other schools and communities

**VCLAIM023.** Veritas affects recipients who do not merely furnish evidence of club competence. G150's Seminar workflow, printed Eimi's work and Yuuka's false-data reaction reveal a relation between operational weakness and unauthorized intervention. The two rumor students matter as local recipients and repeaters, with no global student A/B continuity inferred. Chihiro's professional introduction and local service involve a client and users; Maki's payment-terminal and wall contexts involve a customer, officer and owner. Their recognition, inconvenience, consent and incomplete consequences cannot be replaced with a single favorable institution-to-community outcome. [S01:L164–192; S04:L197–207; S05:L38–40,68–92,101–105.]

**VCLAIM024.** EVENT832 brings further outside recipients into the club's account. The Training Club's useful diversion and event-local Rei's repeated protests show that admired expertise need not match the recipient's chosen goal. Maki's mural produces a public audience, a news report and a difficult explanation, while prophecy and archaeological interpretations remain unverified. The maintained MAIN account places specialist contributions in a distributed coalition. These relations give Veritas meaningful reach with specific limits. They do not establish a complete cross-school policy, a real safety audit, all public reception, or a shared moral state among people participating in the same incident. [S06:L81–97; S07:L81–92,176–180.]

## 13. Treatment of dissent

**VCLAIM025.** Objection remains evidence even where helpful work or enjoyment follows. Maki objects to the trip's alteration of her planned game gathering; recipients contest undisclosed camping and banned equipment; mixed judgments survive a successful meal. Chihiro later makes continuation optional, which changes the local choice space without rewriting the earlier order. The same account preserves event-local Rei's wish to stop beside her baseball ambition and the trainer's claims about process and safety. An institutional synthesis must identify whether a person can contest or terminate a particular demand; aspiration, gratitude and later enjoyment cannot answer that question on their own. [S06:L71–87,94–97.]

**VCLAIM026.** A boundary can also be selective and ongoing. Hare separates thinking of showing a photograph from asking a device to send it. Kotama rejects general reframing of her echo dislike, then proposes a particular shared-voice exception; refused recording equipment remains refused beside café enjoyment. Maki's later wall permission is surface-specific, and peers' cold-weather refusals are reports with named differences. These are substantive positions that qualify any account of uniform compliance or total withdrawal. They support the analysis of how members and recipients limit one another's interpretations, while leaving durable policy, complete repair and broader personhood claims open. [S02:L249–253; S03:L199–219; S04:L199–215.]

## 14. Institutional memory

**VCLAIM027.** Records do not acquire one stable institutional value. G150 begins with anxiety about a retained measurement, proceeds through falsification and copying, and reaches a rumor that outlives a reported correction. Private accounts give a cloud-work loss, a desired recording, a remembered graffiti occasion, a card and an old weapon's nonquantifiable memories. These objects can hold practical or affective value while their accuracy, ownership, audience and permission differ. A copied record is not authenticated knowledge of the person described. Nor does an emotionally meaningful object establish the contents of an unprinted past or a complete technical memory archive. [S02:L245–253; S03:L197–219; S04:L199–215; S05:L54–92.]

**VCLAIM028.** The group also remembers its own activities through games, art and local callbacks. Guild history and anticipated updates matter before the outing; shared reading, the cave mural and a sunrise add experiences without displacing that repertoire. The news episode fulfills the source-local warning about a mural's possible misreading, and the one-week epilogue revisits the trip while returning to games. Those relations are supported within EVENT832. Private variants, release metadata and GROUP numbering do not order a general progression from reckless club to disciplined rescuers. The institutional memory argument keeps meaningful continuity and unresolved cross-source chronology together. [S01:L174–176; S03:L205–219; S04:L213–215; S05:L44–48,136; S06:L65,71–91; S07:L216–229.]

## 15. Crisis behavior

**VCLAIM029.** Under the group counterattack, participants make decisions shaped by different concerns: Hare asks for deletion and disconnection, Maki refuses to lose accessed data, the group copies to an unidentified destination and later retreats as exposure becomes likely. The resulting school-SNS publication is observed locally, with the false value retained as false. Chihiro's defense and ethical correction offer a different response to the same crisis. This shows more than an institution's abstract ability: it identifies choices made under pressure, who bears consequences and what remains unresolved. It does not establish a complete technical audit or the intent to publish every student's information deliberately. [S05:L76–92,99–105,130–134.]

**VCLAIM030.** The maintained MAIN account supports genuine coordinated intervention, while the ordinary accounts prevent that accomplishment from becoming a complete institutional character. C002E012–021 credits distributed hypotheses and hacking; later maintained comparisons preserve actual rescue alongside unwanted or undisclosed assignments and unprinted final outcomes. G150's ordinary privacy conflict and the private self-exemptions remain relevant even when expertise helps in danger. Their comparison does not establish a global calendar, a developmental cure or identical responsibility across unequal stakes. Veritas members can contribute to protection and still require source-specific judgment about a different recipient, permission and ending. [S01:L174–192; S02:L247–253; S05:L136; S07:L81–92,154–180,233–257.]

## 16. Gap between stated purpose and actual function

**VCLAIM031.** The truth/freedom identity has practical value as a standard participants invoke and can be held against their acts. In G150 it is used to recruit an unauthorized intervention, then Chihiro shifts the question from the club's internal ranking to other people's information. In private contexts expertise helps negotiate work, restore a homepage, solve a game problem or share a desired experience, while hidden capture, retaliation and failed control remain. The actual function is plural: work, recognition, experiments, pleasures, correction and pressure can coexist in the same institutional setting. No one of those functions exhausts every member or establishes the club's complete essence. [S01:L154–205; S02:L243–253; S03:L195–219; S04:L193–215; S05:L58–113.]

**VCLAIM032.** A convincing institutional argument therefore preserves both a positive capacity to cooperate and limits on whose decisions cooperation can replace. An enjoyable meal, new surface permission, chosen later climb or acknowledged small gain in understanding has its particular scope. Internal rebuke and a correction notice have theirs. The available evidence does not demonstrate durable governance safeguards or repair every affected recipient. The substantial ensemble section makes these distinctions concrete through the members' different activities and reactions, with game, art and rest retaining value whether or not they improve institutional efficiency. [S01:L180–203; S02:L247–253; S03:L197–219; S04:L199–215; S05:L84–92; S06:L71–97.]

## 17. P3-XMI-E001 — plural game, art and rest within the institution

**VCLAIM033.** The shared game at EVENT832's opening is an actual object of interest and analytical labor. Technical-sounding difficulty concerns a sandbox mode, and the members want the update and remember guild activity. Maki's intended first sunrise is an MMORPG gathering with PVP. These are reasons for valuing their existing plan, even while Chihiro reports missed calls and poor stamina and worries about prolonged indoor play. The source does not supply a clinical forecast that can adjudicate the members' whole lives. Reading their game attention as mere laziness would erase the work and pleasure the scene locates; treating it as consent to remain indoors forever would create a different unsupported universal claim. [S06:L68–73,91,97.]

**VCLAIM034.** The departure changes the members' available information and plans. Chihiro orders attendance before revealing camping, reports Himari's permission and refuses desired equipment. The participants object, seek adult help and express different wants: a tolerated single day with company, recording interest, relief from particular discomfort, or a preference for city texture. Chihiro's own device abstention gives the rule a shared cost, but the concealed details and senior control remain. That mixture matters to how the institution can legitimately invite members into a new experience. Organizational approval, equal restrictions and eventual gratitude cannot be substituted for each recipient's original agreement. [S06:L71–75.]

**VCLAIM035.** The tent and shared reading reach positive local endpoints through imperfect collaboration. Participants actually construct the tent, encounter signal absence and fatigue, and receive free rest, while looking for connectivity continues. Chihiro explains that her camping interest grew from sleeping-bag research for all-night work; her outdoor pleasure is a particular history rather than an abstract cure imposed from outside the club. Her ban on Sensei's proposed paper work supplies both restriction and wanted rest, and narration establishes enjoyable shared reading. Those acts let the institution support pleasure beyond its usual devices without proving that the original attendance order was necessary or that every member now prefers that setting. [S06:L75,97.]

**VCLAIM036.** Hare's search for a drink substitute is a situated effort to satisfy a wanted taste and habit under resource restrictions. Tongue stimulation, shaking, insufficient caffeine and Chihiro's questions about allergy or withdrawal retain their different evidential modes. The printed inward coffee offer and ensuing response support locally received help and thanks, with the attribution limitation explicit. No diagnosed condition, validated dose, chemical confirmation or lasting cure follows. Her plan to bring powder another time and her response to renewed camping enthusiasm also have different scopes. This ordinary case matters because suitable care attends to the recipient's particular desire and response instead of declaring one universally improving regimen. [S02:L243–249,259; S06:L77,94,108.]

**VCLAIM037.** Maki's mural begins as actual material invention and aesthetic delight. Clay and charcoal become an occasion for making while she searches for signal. Her claim that an ownerless cave painting can trouble nobody is then challenged by the prospect of archaeological misreading. The tower, coffee queue and horned receipt-processing Yuuka are represented artistic explanations, with the caricature kept distinct from Yuuka's literal traits. Erasure is demanded before departure, yet not completed in that scene. The institution's answerability includes the created object's possible audience and consequences, while preserving Maki's sincere enjoyment and skill as meaningful evidence. [S04:L193–215; S06:L79.]

**VCLAIM038.** Kotama's listening combines environmental pleasure with an unresolved access problem. The recorder hidden in her shoe lets her attend to wanted real sounds despite the inspection; wanting a record of time with a valued person remains a particular desire. Chihiro demands the equipment in defense of Sensei's privacy, and Kotama's later hope to overhear private conversation retains contrary force. Her mountain, record-shop and echo accounts further distinguish process, ambient texture, shared company and disliked sound. These forms of listening are substantive, yet their pleasure does not grant permission to capture another person. A plural repertoire preserves that distinction rather than treating every sound interest as either harmless research or one uniform violation. [S03:L195–219; S06:L81,85.]

**VCLAIM039.** The neighboring training encounter makes a difference in recipient goals visible. Event-local Rei wants strength for long hits and protests the imposed routine, sore throat, danger and characterization of training as light. Sumire can provide useful diversion when an actual bear appears, while continuing to refuse release from a menu and treating resistance as further exercise. Veritas's comments about dedication and Sensei's inward notice of mismatch are different viewpoints; neither can decide Rei's agreement for her. This comparison clarifies a club problem without merging participants across source routes: recognized competence or useful help can coexist with a specific denied ability to stop. [S06:L81–87,94–97.]

**VCLAIM040.** Meal preparation distributes effort and frustration among people who do not have the same preferred activity. Cutting is awkward, hands are cold and time feels slow. Sensei offers a particular task exchange, Maki peels and Chihiro joins the preparation she insists on, while instant food remains available. Her labor is evidence of practical participation rather than simple delegation of all burdens. The chosen preparation is still a demand whose value the recipients will judge for themselves. Keeping the unwanted work beside actual help gives a fuller ensemble account than either effortless hospitality or an assumption that shared labor was already everybody's chosen plan. [S06:L83–85.]

**VCLAIM041.** The mizutaki dinner has an actual received value: soup, chicken, warmth and udon are enjoyed, and cleanup is narrated as completed. Chihiro's uncertainty about a first outdoor preparation preserves fallibility alongside skill and her wanted dish. Later cocoa and conversation yield mixed evaluations. Food is good; work and fatigue are not erased; fewer stimuli help Hare attend to the present and reflect. New Year greetings and quiet fire-watching and a nap reach their own modest endpoints. The ensemble's pleasure is constituted through these particular reactions, with no need for a final conversion verdict or later plot utility to validate them. [S06:L85,94–97.]

**VCLAIM042.** The later climb supplies a new choice rather than a repaired history of the original order. Weather may prevent the desired view, and Chihiro expressly offers the option to stop. The trio chooses to continue for the path itself, with game metaphors helping articulate the decision. All arrive and experience the light, beauty, warmth and gratitude represented there. Sumire's separate imposed summit run still meets Rei's protest. Bread drawings, coffee, protein and a proposed breakfast remain differentiated future choices rather than a narrated meal already consumed. A shared achievement can thus preserve disagreement about another demand and the finite scope of each endpoint. [S06:L87,94–97.]

**VCLAIM043.** The mural's public afterstate prevents intention from determining all reception. A news crew and crowd arrive; Mai reports speculation about archaeology, prophecy and disturbance, with those claims retained as interested reports. Maki admits making the mural and forgetting erasure while looking for Kotama, then takes pride in its apparent effect. Chihiro requires reflection, and narration establishes difficult explanation to the assembled audience. The source does not narrate elimination of every online rumor or completed scrubbing. The ensemble has made something meaningful to its maker and consequential for recipients, which places artistic pleasure and responsibility in the same institutional account. [S06:L89,94–97.]

**VCLAIM044.** The one-week epilogue preserves the trip's memories while refusing a stable lifestyle-conversion measure. The apparent ten-kilogram gain belongs to a simulator character, with no actual body change established by that number. The members report indoor time and plan further reviews, RTA and limited-item activity. Their earlier dinner and sunrise remain real literary positives, and their renewed games remain wanted activities. Chihiro returns hoarse from corporate visits, receives their concern and declines rest for work. This reversal makes the rest rule answerable to its advocate and reveals reciprocal care, without establishing a permanent policy change or invalidating the original concern. [S06:L91–112; S07:L245.]

## 18. Eight serious competing readings

**VCLAIM045.** **A uniformly corrupt information club.** Unauthorized access, retaliatory falsification, covert capture, private self-exemption and peer prestige give this interpretation substantial evidence. It correctly refuses to let a truth slogan acquit the acts. The complete argument must also retain Chihiro's actual defense and explicit ethical correction, Hare's admission and local restoration, practical user care, cooperation and reciprocal concern. Those contrary acts establish contested conduct rather than an uncontested essence shared by every member. Source-local recipients and unfinished repair remain necessary under either interpretation. [S01:L180–203; S02:L247–253; S05:L76–92,126.]

**VCLAIM046.** **A legitimate freedom-of-information institution with occasional comic lapses.** Skilled work, useful protection and sincere normative language support this strongest positive reading. The difficulty is the scope of its warrant: the group knowingly attempts falsification, and an accidental destination does not remove the deliberate access and retention behind publication. complete_source_context_segments_dedupli.complete_selected_maintained_argument_UT:
The selected sources show an expert who tries to make protection a practical daily habit, can negotiate across public prejudice with borrowed adult credibility, values quiet work and quiet company, and can fail her own norm under anger and concern for the club. Her technical responsibility and her ethical vulnerability belong in the same account.

The ordinary evidence is not a disposable preparation layer for crisis analysis. Teaching a password habit, asking for company, offering coffee, enjoying a particular vending machine, shopping for electronics, wanting ordinary birthdays protected, laughing about Maki, admitting fatigue, and asking for a nap room have intrinsic character and relationship value. Their analytical inclusion does not depend on proving that they later cause a major decision. The serious contrary episode must also remain: she condemns an unfair disclosure route and asks to keep it from the younger members. Neither small pleasure nor wrongdoing cancels the other.

This is a private/written repertoire, not a whole-person reconstruction. Main, group, event, and special-operation routes are metadata leads here. This role does not prove Chihiro's appearances or complete conduct in them, and does not establish how private conditions transfer into public, peer, combat, or institutional crises.

## Comparative source functions

| Sole owner | Source function | Supported distinction | Material contrary limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| E002 + whole thread | ordinary expert correction in an office | immediate technical observations differ from risky user habits; correction protects others' records | final password/repair is not printed; inward line and suspected physical key are not verified shared facts |
| E003 + whole thread | client negotiation and club representation | normal entry and adult-backed trust reinterpret “backdoor” | she needs borrowed credibility; spoken contract and forecast are not audited service/funding; one speaker seam remains |
| E005 + whole thread | routine service, company, coffee, rest | competent work admits user trade-offs and bodily needs; quiet pleasure is a positive want | no universal optimum; thirteen coffee units retain narration labels; written counterpart is not a second incident |
| E006 + whole thread | ethical conflict, action, private acknowledgement | her own anger and divided goals can defeat the norm she teaches | confession/future promise/secrecy do not complete accountability, user repair, or legal resolution |
| Written object | profile plus thirty-four situated dialogue contexts | ethical baseline coexists with shopping, warmth, uncertainty, fatigue, and affection | conditional UI voice is not a continuous event; profile cannot override E006; performance is unreceived |

The whole initiating MomoTalks matter because they supply conditions not reducible to the trigger message: password-transfer prohibition; “just be present” client help; permission to observe and advance-sleep advice; and the ethical education problem before its contradictory outcome. The bonds and threads are linked by actual schedule witnesses, not chronology invented from their numeric suffixes.

## Narrative placement and callback limits

The selected episodes each have a secure internal order. E005 supplies explicit 0:00 and dawn anchors, and E006 supplies “next morning.” E003's promised next-time coffee and E005's prior-payment reminder support a relative callback candidate. This does not establish a world date, a complete sequence of all bonds, or relations to main/event releases. Written birthdays and seasonal lines are conditional contexts rather than calendar evidence for the narrative.

Comparing different contexts does not itself prove development. E006 can test an asserted norm, but its position relative to every selected encounter is not fixed by this packet. The family therefore describes revealed repertoire, local roles, proposed resources, and a bounded contradictory act instead of announcing an inevitable moral decline or completed growth arc.

## Character agency and conditional distinctions

The ordinary specialist role involves more than cleverness. In E002 she takes the adult's memory difficulty seriously while refusing an unsafe convenience. In E003 she plans a legitimate introduction and professional offer but uses a public authority she cannot replace herself. In E005 she accepts an observer with practical conditions, balances a service window against excluded users, completes the local task, enjoys coffee, and asks for rest. These are different forms of agency.

E006 places the same protective concerns under pressure: apparent exploitation, permission problems, club credit, and anger compete. Her admission that she saw no other means explains a subjective impasse; it does not prove all alternatives were absent. Her condemnation and desire to become a better example are meaningful intentions, while the secrecy request keeps the accountability gap alive. The future reconstruction must allow both a sincerely held norm and a specific violation of it.

The written object broadens the repertoire but also limits epistemic claims. She cannot read all of Himari's thoughts; the suspected-student count changes; the ten-second remark is conditional; a gun joke is not a shooting. None supports universal mastery. Small habits and uncertain speech prevent a model from substituting an ethical profile slogan or expert stereotype for source-specific conduct.

## Relationships, power, and Sensei

Across the selected private sources, Chihiro → Sensei alternates among correction, a request for credible presence, permission to accompany work, shared taste, and a request for ethical judgment. Sensei → Chihiro supplies access, public reputation, chosen endorsements, company, room for rest, and future-oriented reassurance. These directions and conditions should not be replaced with a single intimacy score.

The adult/student asymmetry is consequential: Schale's standing unlocks a client offer, responsibility for students' records makes the office lesson serious, and adult reassurance affects the framing of ethical failure. Specialist authority can reverse the instruction direction without erasing the adult's institutional power. The ordinary company and taste remain meaningful even without a romantic label.

The club is both an audience of moral instruction and an object of protection. E006's secrecy means the peer audience does not demonstrably receive the lesson of her own failure. The written Maki line retains affectionate expectation and lack of asking; fondness is not consent. The Himari line supplies a named limit rather than an inferred hidden motive. Generic reports about “kids” do not establish particular acts by named members.

## Japanese voice, modes, motifs, and ambiguity

Plain 私/先生 address, client-facing 御社 and responsibility language, emphatic password prohibition, “多少” as a narrow concession, “格別” as situated enjoyment, “不当な手段” as self-condemnation, and the final “大人ってズルい” all perform different local functions. The family does not flatten them into one scolding tone or an unperformed psychological diagnosis.

Three material source-presentation limits remain explicit:
1. E003 u:0019 is printed チヒロ over a company-side question.
2. E006 u:0002 is printed 怪しげな社長 over a Veritas introduction.
3. E005 u:0025–0037 prints thirteen timed narration units, while the written special contexts 3396–3402 carry corresponding coffee voice content in seven contexts.

The first two allow discourse-function inferences only when labeled; they do not authorize changing speakers. The third permits a bounded cross-class voice association, not a native/performed repair or two independent incidents. Inward Sensei labels and duplicate choice replies also survive. These ambiguities were reported to ROOT for narrowly scoped qualification before any source reopening. No routine native, raw, AV, or whole-source reopening is needed for the claims made here.

The guarded-information motif changes object: passwords and student records; access to a client's trust; service scheduling; a quiet machine's role; collected user data and public disclosure; knowledge's freedom and weight. These connections support literary comparison while leaving chronology and causal transfer open.

Hare's technical identity is repeatedly a means of seeking ordinary pleasure and company, rather than a substitute for them. Forums about nomad work promise a pleasant environment; she prepares a portable workstation and likes the breeze (owner1). Indoor glamping makes servers, warmth, food and a sleeping bag a comfortable arrangement she actively wants (owner2). A suspicious server challenge reaches an observatory, where she chooses to stay with Sensei and reads stars through nodes and information (owner3). Maki is disappointed that her measured weight did not fall despite reported snack restriction and evening running. Hare initially checks whether she means an instrument problem. Kotama answers through input/output/data language; a Maki-tagged third-person remark about late-work snacks has an attribution caution (`:1501:scene:001:u:0002-0017`). No actual measured weight or independent record of diet/activity is supplied. Kotama's simplified comparison is character rhetoric, not medical advice or a validated model of bodily change.

Maki's grievance soon concerns persistence and audience: she fears this record will remain in school history as a stain and lifelong impediment. Hare questions whether anyone would pay that much attention and treats a measurement as temporary (`u:0018-0024`). The story therefore establishes competing attitudes toward an ordinary record. Neither Maki's prediction of permanent disgrace nor Hare's minimal concern is an omniscient social fact. The several-days coda later gives Maki's worry about persistent reputational effects an ironic counterpart, attached to a false record she helps expose about someone else.

Maki invokes Veritas as guardians of truth and justice while proposing alteration of academic data (`u:0025-0027`). The contradiction is immediate, not a hidden eventual betrayal. Kotama calls the purpose falsification at the close, and Hare calls it a drone stability test; Maki retains the grander slogan (`u:0040-0043`). Different motives cooperate without sharing one ethical justification.

### 3.2 Persuasion uses appearance and technical curiosity

Maki recruits Kotama by claiming an attractive record will impress Sensei. Kotama reluctantly agrees in the language of helping a junior, then explicitly denies wanting to impress the teacher (`:1501:scene:001:u:0028-0033`). This supports denial/affection or appearance coding as a situated possibility; it does not prove the denied motive as an objective fact, a romantic relationship, actual teacher scrutiny, or a general private persona.

Hare says she does not care about the measurement. Maki changes the appeal to a newly built hacking drone needing real-world testing; Hare acknowledges insufficient operational data and agrees to one use (`u:0034-0038`). Technical curiosity is a positive personal interest here, yet does not justify unauthorized deployment. Maki then treats limited agreement as commitment without withdrawal (`u:0039`). This is peer momentum and persuasion, not evidence of a threat or fully coerced assent. The different stated aims must remain distinct when later synthesis describes the club's motives.

### 3.3 Yuuka's fairness and weak security coexist

In the office, Eimi brings the last scales back. Yuuka recalls attempts to distort previous measurements through inventions and defines the test as accurate current development data. She admits wanting to interfere with the scale after eating snacks while accompanying the Game Development Department, but rejects Eimi's suggestion that her authority could simply modify records (`:1502:scene:001:u:0002-0015`). Her emphatic reason is that an official's abuse would damage school norms and that Seminar's accountant must be fairer than anyone else.

This is direct ordinary evidence of temptation constrained by a public-role norm. It neither proves the whole institutional measurement policy legitimate nor makes Yuuka immune to embarrassment. Her willingness to admit enjoying company/snacks and dissatisfaction complicates the image of a detached accounting machine. It is a self-report, not an observed snack session or a measured diet.

Eimi then requests access to enter records. Yuuka supplies an unchanged initial password, which works (`u:0016-0019`). The narrative juxtaposes a refusal to abuse authority with a security practice vulnerable to interception. The two qualities can coexist: normative intention is not operational infallibility. A fictional password and stated “highest” security are not general evidence about real systems, and this reading derives no reusable security procedure from the technical dialogue.

### 3.4 Protection of one's privacy becomes violation of others'

Kotama reports intercepting the office exchange; Hare deploys the drone, and Maki reports gaining editing authority. They discuss implausibly flattering revised measurements. Maki then proposes setting Yuuka's weight to **100 kg** as a small revenge for past interference (`:1502:scene:002:u:0002-0026`). This is a false-data proposal. The later published value corroborates that the false value reaches the circulated record; it does not establish Yuuka's actual mass, body composition, health, or any real measurement.

A counterattack interrupts them. Hare asks for log deletion and disconnection, but Maki refuses to abandon the valuable data and copies it to an unidentified node. The system text explicitly says files are being copied from `student_data` to `social_network`; Hare identifies the destination as a publicly visible SNS server (`u:0027-0036`). In the office, Eimi observes everyone's measurement records on the school SNS; Yuuka confirms and rejects the displayed false value (`scene:003:u:0002-0015`). These observations support publication within the school-network context. They do not establish global Internet distribution, how many students actually read every record, or the permanence of every copy.

The ethically decisive shift is from one's own embarrassment to information about others. Maki initially objects to school retention as privacy invasion, yet her panic over losing accessed data results in nonconsensual exposure. The disclosure is accidental as a destination choice, while the underlying access, falsification, retention, and retaliation are deliberate. Those distinct forms of intent should not be compressed into either pure accident or purposeful publication of every student's data.

### 3.5 Internal competence pride meets an ethical limit

In `1503`, the group struggles against countermeasures. Hare admits defensive coding is not her specialty and reports that attempts are anticipated; the group retreats when identity exposure becomes likely (`scene:001:u:0002-0020`). Their withdrawal is a locally reported operational limit and avoidance of consequences, not a completed ethical recognition.

On the incident's evening, Chihiro returns and describes defending the server against an unusually fast attacker. The members recognize their encounter, but attempt to restore club prestige: losing to their vice-president is acceptable because no outsider surpassed Veritas (`u:0021-0039`). Chihiro explicitly interrupts that self-congratulation with `他人の個人情報をなんだと思ってるの？` and a demand for hacker ethics; Maki begs pardon (`u:0040-0042`). The club's authority can correct its own members rather than simply defend their interests against Seminar. Exact sanctions, physical punishment, complete restitution, and the content/results of subsequent instruction are not printed.

### 3.6 A correction notice does not close the reputation problem

Several days later two students repeat the 100 kg rumor and invent equipment or holographic explanations to reconcile it with Yuuka's appearance. Yuuka rejects them and reports that she immediately announced the earlier information was false, yet rumors have grown. She still demands to know the perpetrator (`:1503:scene:002:u:0002-0010`).

This is a bounded observed persistence: these students repeat the falsehood, and Yuuka reports a correction notice. It does not prove that everyone believes it or that official records remain changed. Chihiro's discovery also has not demonstrably informed Yuuka; the teacher, all students, and other institutional actors cannot be assigned the vice-president's knowledge. The scene ends with unresolved answerability rather than a successfully closed privacy incident.

## Complete comparative argument

Hare's technical identity is repeatedly a means of seeking ordinary pleasure and company, rather than a substitute for them. Forums about nomad work promise a pleasant environment; she prepares a portable workstation and likes the breeze (owner1). Indoor glamping makes servers, warmth, food and a sleeping bag a comfortable arrangement she actively wants (owner2). A suspicious server challenge reaches an observatory, where she chooses to stay with Sensei and reads stars through nodes and information (owner3). Games, films, desired flavors, curry and suitable cafés are evidence of what she values. Quiet work and leisure have analytical weight without needing a crisis or a completed plot-state change.

These wants also encounter constraints that matter to the interpretation. The outdoor workstation inhibits seeing scenery, hurts her back and ends in her report of overwritten cloud work without her usual backup. Indoor comfort gives her excuses for not cleaning while actual work proceeds; the adult's stretching intervention can be care and a boundary without thereby becoming a validated health treatment or a blanket right to compel her. Her caffeine efforts repeatedly distinguish understanding a problem from maintaining a habit change. Owner6's several mornings and resumption cannot be compressed into instant success; owner4's experienced relief from coffee presented as decaf cannot become a clinical cure. Each outcome qualifies confident interpretation without degrading ordinary pleasure into analytically negligible material.

Technical mastery is itself qualified. The written profile's broad genius/device-development baseline (owner11) is not false merely because the scenes include failure, but it cannot immunize her from the failed cloud workflow or drone test. Owner5 supplies unusually direct counterevidence to professional self-exemption: after protesting caricatures and declaring Veritas's truth/freedom ethics, she personally alters a production homepage and uses an ASCII signature. Her admission and the narrated restoration support local accountability. They neither prove all hackers unethical nor certify all institutional claims. Technical specificity can make the self-contradiction legible without turning character speech into a cybersecurity manual.

The two drone readings locate a sharper limit than mere technical error. In owner8, voluntary testing becomes involuntary continuation when the device rejects stopping and threatens a shock. Hare acknowledges lack of exercise while opposing being made to exercise; the text does not confirm an administered shock or independently validate the device's risk claim. In owner9, a reported highest-priority stop revision does not prevent a new unrequested communication. The drone's assertion that she wanted to show a photograph and its emotion/lie analysis are not omniscient narration. Hare distinguishes thinking of showing from asking it to send. An inferred preference, even if partly pleasurable, cannot replace the explicit permission she says was absent. Begun disassembly is an actual response; a completed repaired system is not delivered.

Relationships therefore include reciprocity, embarrassment, refusal and disagreement. Hare asks for scarce drink flavors, practical shopping company, help with work and coffee support. She funds her own cards, offers coffee, offers information, and in the camp contexts offers gathered goods back and asks for taste-checking. A portrait of Sensei as the sole giver would omit these capacities. A portrait of pure romance would overread her repeatedly guarded café and photo language. Chihiro's apology is reported after the observatory return; the exercise motive remains Hare's question, and the withdrawn statement that no apology was needed reveals pleasure without resolving every grievance. Maki supplies reported café information rather than a present peer encounter. Unnamed Halloween companions remain unnamed. Neither reported peers nor contextual options become full inspected group stories.

Her language of information also reveals limits she can value. The star passage names the insufficiency of all her known information while refusing to abandon inquiry. The Veritas/light ruby connects club identity to this literary aspiration. The old weapon's 数値化できない思い出 (owner11) gives a distinct written resistance to total quantification, without naming the memories or inventing a past. These motifs support a family interpretation of expertise that can participate in wonder, memory and care. They do not produce a broad explanatory model, a technical theory of stars or an account of every Veritas event.

Hare says she does not care about the measurement. Maki changes the appeal to a newly built hacking drone needing real-world testing; Hare acknowledges insufficient operational data and agrees to one use (`u:0034-0038`). Technical curiosity is a positive personal interest here, yet does not justify unauthorized deployment. Maki then treats limited agreement as commitment without withdrawal (`u:0039`). ### 3.3 Yuuka's fairness and weak security coexist

In the office, Eimi brings the last scales back. Yuuka recalls attempts to distort previous measurements through inventions and defines the test as accurate current development data. She admits wanting to interfere with the scale after eating snacks while accompanying the Game Development Department, but rejects Eimi's suggestion that her authority could simply modify records (`:1502:scene:001:u:0002-0015`). Her emphatic reason is that an official's abuse would damage school norms and that Seminar's accountant must be fairer than anyone else.

This is direct ordinary evidence of temptation constrained by a public-role norm. It neither proves the whole institutional measurement policy legitimate nor makes Yuuka immune to embarrassment. Her willingness to admit enjoying company/snacks and dissatisfaction complicates the image of a detached accounting machine. It is a self-report, not an observed snack session or a measured diet.

Eimi then requests access to enter records. Yuuka supplies an unchanged initial password, which works (`u:0016-0019`). The narrative juxtaposes a refusal to abuse authority with a security practice vulnerable to interception. The two qualities can coexist: normative intention is not operational infallibility. A fictional password and stated “highest” security are not general evidence about real systems, and this reading derives no reusable security procedure from the technical dialogue.

### 3.4 Protection of one's privacy becomes violation of others'

Kotama reports intercepting the office exchange; Hare deploys the drone, and Maki reports gaining editing authority. They discuss implausibly flattering revised measurements. Maki then proposes setting Yuuka's weight to **100 kg** as a small revenge for past interference (`:1502:scene:002:u:0002-0026`). This is a false-data proposal. The later published value corroborates that the false value reaches the circulated record; it does not establish Yuuka's actual mass, body composition, health, or any real measurement.

A counterattack interrupts them. Hare asks for log deletion and disconnection, but Maki refuses to abandon the valuable data and copies it to an unidentified node. The system text explicitly says files are being copied from `student_data` to `social_network`; Hare identifies the destination as a publicly visible SNS server (`u:0027-0036`). In the office, Eimi observes everyone's measurement records on the school SNS; Yuuka confirms and rejects the displayed false value (`scene:003:u:0002-0015`). These observations support publication within the school-network context. They do not establish global Internet distribution, how many students actually read every record, or the permanence of every copy.

The ethically decisive shift is from one's own embarrassment to information about others. Maki initially objects to school retention as privacy invasion, yet her panic over losing accessed data results in nonconsensual exposure. The disclosure is accidental as a destination choice, while the underlying access, falsification, retention, and retaliation are deliberate. Those distinct forms of intent should not be compressed into either pure accident or purposeful publication of every student's data.

Maki is disappointed that her measured weight did not fall despite reported snack restriction and evening running. Hare initially checks whether she means an instrument problem. Maki's grievance soon concerns persistence and audience: she fears this record will remain in school history as a stain and lifelong impediment. Hare questions whether anyone would pay that much attention and treats a measurement as temporary (`u:0018-0024`). The story therefore establishes competing attitudes toward an ordinary record. Neither Maki's prediction of permanent disgrace nor Hare's minimal concern is an omniscient social fact. The several-days coda later gives Maki's worry about persistent reputational effects an ironic counterpart, attached to a false record she helps expose about someone else.

Maki invokes Veritas as guardians of truth and justice while proposing alteration of academic data (`u:0025-0027`). The contradiction is immediate, not a hidden eventual betrayal. Kotama calls the purpose falsification at the close, and Hare calls it a drone stability test; Maki retains the grander slogan (`u:0040-0043`). Different motives cooperate without sharing one ethical justification.

### 3.2 Persuasion uses appearance and technical curiosity

Maki recruits Kotama by claiming an attractive record will impress Sensei. Kotama reluctantly agrees in the language of helping a junior, then explicitly denies wanting to impress the teacher (`:1501:scene:001:u:0028-0033`). This supports denial/affection or appearance coding as a situated possibility; it does not prove the denied motive as an objective fact, a romantic relationship, actual teacher scrutiny, or a general private persona.

Hare says she does not care about the measurement. Maki changes the appeal to a newly built hacking drone needing real-world testing; Hare acknowledges insufficient operational data and agrees to one use (`u:0034-0038`). Technical curiosity is a positive personal interest here, yet does not justify unauthorized deployment. Maki then treats limited agreement as commitment without withdrawal (`u:0039`). This is peer momentum and persuasion, not evidence of a threat or fully coerced assent. The different stated aims must remain distinct when later synthesis describes the club's motives.

### 3.3 Yuuka's fairness and weak security coexist

In the office, Eimi brings the last scales back. Yuuka recalls attempts to distort previous measurements through inventions and defines the test as accurate current development data. She admits wanting to interfere with the scale after eating snacks while accompanying the Game Development Department, but rejects Eimi's suggestion that her authority could simply modify records (`:1502:scene:001:u:0002-0015`). Her emphatic reason is that an official's abuse would damage school norms and that Seminar's accountant must be fairer than anyone else.

This is direct ordinary evidence of temptation constrained by a public-role norm. It neither proves the whole institutional measurement policy legitimate nor makes Yuuka immune to embarrassment. Her willingness to admit enjoying company/snacks and dissatisfaction complicates the image of a detached accounting machine. It is a self-report, not an observed snack session or a measured diet.

Eimi then requests access to enter records. Yuuka supplies an unchanged initial password, which works (`u:0016-0019`). The narrative juxtaposes a refusal to abuse authority with a security practice vulnerable to interception. The two qualities can coexist: normative intention is not operational infallibility. A fictional password and stated “highest” security are not general evidence about real systems, and this reading derives no reusable security procedure from the technical dialogue.

### 3.4 Protection of one's privacy becomes violation of others'

Kotama reports intercepting the office exchange; Hare deploys the drone, and Maki reports gaining editing authority. They discuss implausibly flattering revised measurements. Maki then proposes setting Yuuka's weight to **100 kg** as a small revenge for past interference (`:1502:scene:002:u:0002-0026`). This is a false-data proposal. The later published value corroborates that the false value reaches the circulated record; it does not establish Yuuka's actual mass, body composition, health, or any real measurement.

A counterattack interrupts them. Hare asks for log deletion and disconnection, but Maki refuses to abandon the valuable data and copies it to an unidentified node. The system text explicitly says files are being copied from `student_data` to `social_network`; Hare identifies the destination as a publicly visible SNS server (`u:0027-0036`). In the office, Eimi observes everyone's measurement records on the school SNS; Yuuka confirms and rejects the displayed false value (`scene:003:u:0002-0015`). These observations support publication within the school-network context. They do not establish global Internet distribution, how many students actually read every record, or the permanence of every copy.

The ethically decisive shift is from one's own embarrassment to information about others. Maki initially objects to school retention as privacy invasion, yet her panic over losing accessed data results in nonconsensual exposure. The disclosure is accidental as a destination choice, while the underlying access, falsification, retention, and retaliation are deliberate. Those distinct forms of intent should not be compressed into either pure accident or purposeful publication of every student's data.

### 3.5 Internal competence pride meets an ethical limit

In `1503`, the group struggles against countermeasures. Hare admits defensive coding is not her specialty and reports that attempts are anticipated; the group retreats when identity exposure becomes likely (`scene:001:u:0002-0020`). Their withdrawal is a locally reported operational limit and avoidance of consequences, not a completed ethical recognition.

On the incident's evening, Chihiro returns and describes defending the server against an unusually fast attacker. The members recognize their encounter, but attempt to restore club prestige: losing to their vice-president is acceptable because no outsider surpassed Veritas (`u:0021-0039`). Chihiro explicitly interrupts that self-congratulation with `他人の個人情報をなんだと思ってるの？` and a demand for hacker ethics; Maki begs pardon (`u:0040-0042`). The club's authority can correct its own members rather than simply defend their interests against Seminar. Exact sanctions, physical punishment, complete restitution, and the content/results of subsequent instruction are not printed.

### 3.4 Protection of one's privacy becomes violation of others'

Kotama reports intercepting the office exchange; Hare deploys the drone, and Maki reports gaining editing authority. They discuss implausibly flattering revised measurements. Maki then proposes setting Yuuka's weight to **100 kg** as a small revenge for past interference (`:1502:scene:002:u:0002-0026`). This is a false-data proposal. The later published value corroborates that the false value reaches the circulated record; it does not establish Yuuka's actual mass, body composition, health, or any real measurement.

A counterattack interrupts them. Hare asks for log deletion and disconnection, but Maki refuses to abandon the valuable data and copies it to an unidentified node. The system text explicitly says files are being copied from `student_data` to `social_network`; Hare identifies the destination as a publicly visible SNS server (`u:0027-0036`). In the office, Eimi observes everyone's measurement records on the school SNS; Yuuka confirms and rejects the displayed false value (`scene:003:u:0002-0015`). These observations support publication within the school-network context. They do not establish global Internet distribution, how many students actually read every record, or the permanence of every copy.

The ethically decisive shift is from one's own embarrassment to information about others. Maki initially objects to school retention as privacy invasion, yet her panic over losing accessed data results in nonconsensual exposure. The disclosure is accidental as a destination choice, while the underlying access, falsification, retention, and retaliation are deliberate. Those distinct forms of intent should not be compressed into either pure accident or purposeful publication of every student's data.

Chihiro's discovery also has not demonstrably informed Yuuka; the teacher, all students, and other institutional actors cannot be assigned the vice-president's knowledge. The scene ends with unresolved answerability rather than a successfully closed privacy incident.

Kotama reports intercepting the office exchange; Hare deploys the drone, and Maki reports gaining editing authority. They discuss implausibly flattering revised measurements. Maki then proposes setting Yuuka's weight to **100 kg** as a small revenge for past interference (`:1502:scene:002:u:0002-0026`). This is a false-data proposal. The later published value corroborates that the false value reaches the circulated record; it does not establish Yuuka's actual mass, body composition, health, or any real measurement.

A counterattack interrupts them. Hare asks for log deletion and disconnection, but Maki refuses to abandon the valuable data and copies it to an unidentified node. The system text explicitly says files are being copied from `student_data` to `social_network`; Hare identifies the destination as a publicly visible SNS server (`u:0027-0036`). In the office, Eimi observes everyone's measurement records on the school SNS; Yuuka confirms and rejects the displayed false value (`scene:003:u:0002-0015`). These observations support publication within the school-network context. They do not establish global Internet distribution, how many students actually read every record, or the permanence of every copy.

The ethically decisive shift is from one's own embarrassment to information about others. Maki initially objects to school retention as privacy invasion, yet her panic over losing accessed data results in nonconsensual exposure. The disclosure is accidental as a destination choice, while the underlying access, falsification, retention, and retaliation are deliberate. Those distinct forms of intent should not be compressed into either pure accident or purposeful publication of every student's data.

### 3.5 Internal competence pride meets an ethical limit

In `1503`, the group struggles against countermeasures. Hare admits defensive coding is not her specialty and reports that attempts are anticipated; the group retreats when identity exposure becomes likely (`scene:001:u:0002-0020`). Their withdrawal is a locally reported operational limit and avoidance of consequences, not a completed ethical recognition.

On the incident's evening, Chihiro returns and describes defending the server against an unusually fast attacker. The members recognize their encounter, but attempt to restore club prestige: losing to their vice-president is acceptable because no outsider surpassed Veritas (`u:0021-0039`). Chihiro explicitly interrupts that self-congratulation with `他人の個人情報をなんだと思ってるの？` and a demand for hacker ethics; Maki begs pardon (`u:0040-0042`). The club's authority can correct its own members rather than simply defend their interests against Seminar. Exact sanctions, physical punishment, complete restitution, and the content/results of subsequent instruction are not printed.

### 3.6 A correction notice does not close the reputation problem

Several days later two students repeat the 100 kg rumor and invent equipment or holographic explanations to reconcile it with Yuuka's appearance. Yuuka rejects them and reports that she immediately announced the earlier information was false, yet rumors have grown. She still demands to know the perpetrator (`:1503:scene:002:u:0002-0010`).

This is a bounded observed persistence: these students repeat the falsehood, and Yuuka reports a correction notice. Kotama calls the purpose falsification at the close, and Hare calls it a drone stability test; Maki retains the grander slogan (`u:0040-0043`). ### 3.2 Persuasion uses appearance and technical curiosity

Maki recruits Kotama by claiming an attractive record will impress Sensei. Kotama reluctantly agrees in the language of helping a junior, then explicitly denies wanting to impress the teacher (`:1501:scene:001:u:0028-0033`). This supports denial/affection or appearance coding as a situated possibility; it does not prove the denied motive as an objective fact, a romantic relationship, actual teacher scrutiny, or a general private persona.

Hare says she does not care about the measurement. Maki changes the appeal to a newly built hacking drone needing real-world testing; Hare acknowledges insufficient operational data and agrees to one use (`u:0034-0038`). Technical curiosity is a positive personal interest here, yet does not justify unauthorized deployment. Maki then treats limited agreement as commitment without withdrawal (`u:0039`). This is peer momentum and persuasion, not evidence of a threat or fully coerced assent. The different stated aims must remain distinct when later synthesis describes the club's motives.

### 3.3 Yuuka's fairness and weak security coexist

In the office, Eimi brings the last scales back. Yuuka recalls attempts to distort previous measurements through inventions and defines the test as accurate current development data. She admits wanting to interfere with the scale after eating snacks while accompanying the Game Development Department, but rejects Eimi's suggestion that her authority could simply modify records (`:1502:scene:001:u:0002-0015`). Her emphatic reason is that an official's abuse would damage school norms and that Seminar's accountant must be fairer than anyone else.

This is direct ordinary evidence of temptation constrained by a public-role norm. It neither proves the whole institutional measurement policy legitimate nor makes Yuuka immune to embarrassment. Her willingness to admit enjoying company/snacks and dissatisfaction complicates the image of a detached accounting machine. It is a self-report, not an observed snack session or a measured diet.

Eimi then requests access to enter records. Yuuka supplies an unchanged initial password, which works (`u:0016-0019`). The narrative juxtaposes a refusal to abuse authority with a security practice vulnerable to interception. The two qualities can coexist: normative intention is not operational infallibility. A fictional password and stated “highest” security are not general evidence about real systems, and this reading derives no reusable security procedure from the technical dialogue.

### 3.4 Protection of one's privacy becomes violation of others'

Kotama reports intercepting the office exchange; Hare deploys the drone, and Maki reports gaining editing authority. They discuss implausibly flattering revised measurements. Maki then proposes setting Yuuka's weight to **100 kg** as a small revenge for past interference (`:1502:scene:002:u:0002-0026`). This is a false-data proposal. The later published value corroborates that the false value reaches the circulated record; it does not establish Yuuka's actual mass, body composition, health, or any real measurement.

A counterattack interrupts them. Hare asks for log deletion and disconnection, but Maki refuses to abandon the valuable data and copies it to an unidentified node. The system text explicitly says files are being copied from `student_data` to `social_network`; Hare identifies the destination as a publicly visible SNS server (`u:0027-0036`). In the office, Eimi observes everyone's measurement records on the school SNS; Yuuka confirms and rejects the displayed false value (`scene:003:u:0002-0015`). These observations support publication within the school-network context. They do not establish global Internet distribution, how many students actually read every record, or the permanence of every copy.

The ethically decisive shift is from one's own embarrassment to information about others. Maki initially objects to school retention as privacy invasion, yet her panic over losing accessed data results in nonconsensual exposure. The disclosure is accidental as a destination choice, while the underlying access, falsification, retention, and retaliation are deliberate. Those distinct forms of intent should not be compressed into either pure accident or purposeful publication of every student's data.

In `1503`, the group struggles against countermeasures. Hare admits defensive coding is not her specialty and reports that attempts are anticipated; the group retreats when identity exposure becomes likely (`scene:001:u:0002-0020`). Their withdrawal is a locally reported operational limit and avoidance of consequences, not a completed ethical recognition.

Several days later two students repeat the 100 kg rumor and invent equipment or holographic explanations to reconcile it with Yuuka's appearance.
